title: Conchiglie al pesto
subtitle: Shell pasta with basil pesto
excerpt: Conchiglie al pesto is shell pasta tossed with fresh basil pesto. The curved shells catch the sauce inside, giving each mouthful a concentrated hit of basil, garlic, and olive oil. This is one of the quickest pasta dishes there is: the time is all in making the pesto, which takes under 5 minutes in a food processor.
sourceNotes: Italian home-cooking tradition. Pesto alla genovese with various pasta shapes is eaten throughout Italy. Shell pasta (conchiglie) is popular for pesto because its curved shape traps the sauce. Methods drawn from Marcella Hazan, Essentials of Classic Italian Cooking (1992).

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Pesto can be made a day ahead and stored in the fridge, covered with a thin film of olive oil to prevent browning.

glossaryTerms.definition: Shell-shaped pasta; the name means 'shells' in Italian; the curved, ridged surface traps sauces inside the shell for a concentrated burst of flavour.

content.text: Conchiglie al pesto is simple to prepare: shell-shaped

tossed with a fresh basil pesto. The shells cup the sauce in their interior so each one carries a small pool of green, fragrant oil. Making the pesto takes about 5 minutes; everything else is boiling pasta.

Blend the basil, {{garlic}} of garlic, Parmesan, Pecorino, and a pinch of salt in a food processor until finely chopped. With the motor running, pour in {{extra-virgin-olive-oil}} of extra-virgin olive oil in a thin stream until the pesto is slightly textured and bright green. Taste for salt.

Cook {{pasta-dried}} of conchiglie in a large pot of well-salted boiling water until al dente. Reserve a mug of pasta water, then drain. Return the pasta to the pot off the heat. Add the pesto and toss, adding pasta water a tablespoon at a time until the pesto flows easily and coats each shell. Serve with more Parmesan.

items.symptom: Pesto is brown rather than bright green
items.cause: Basil oxidised from heat or blending too fast.
items.fix: Use cold basil straight from the fridge. Blend in short pulses rather than running the processor continuously. Serve quickly once the pesto is made.

items.symptom: Pesto is too thick to toss
items.fix: Add pasta water a tablespoon at a time and toss until the pesto loosens to a flowing consistency.
Season more generously and add a little more grated cheese. Pesto is punchy by nature.

content.text: Pesto is from Genoa, but it is eaten with dozens of pasta shapes across Italy. Shell pasta is a particularly good vehicle because the ridged cups prevent the sauce from sliding off. At its best in summer, when basil is in season and fragrant, this is a dish that can be made in the time it takes to bring a pot of water to the boil.
